### Project Name

agentproto-privacy-preserving-dialog-recovery

### Project Description

Privacy-Preserving Cross-Domain Agent Dialog Recovery is an open-source research prototype for investigating reliable multi-agent communication across independent administrative domains.

The implementation explores how agent conversations can recover from gateway failures while preserving domain-specific dialog identifiers and enforcing authorization requirements.

The project includes persistent recovery state, cryptographically protected recovery tickets, failure-injection experiments, operation-ledger integrity checks, and reproducible evaluation tools.

The public repository currently contains version 0.2.1, with documented experiments, regression tests, and implementation changes.

The project is independently maintained and remains at the research-prototype stage. Its objective is to provide reusable technical evidence and eventually enable broader interoperability and reliability testing.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

The project supports the Agentic AI Foundation's objectives of improving the security, interoperability, and reliability of agentic AI systems.

It focuses on a practical challenge for multi-agent architectures: safely resuming cross-domain conversations after infrastructure failures without unnecessarily exposing globally linkable identifiers.

The implementation can serve as an experimental reference for evaluating recovery mechanisms, authorization boundaries, and privacy-security tradeoffs across independently operated agent systems.


### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

The project explores reliability and security questions relevant to agent communication systems such as the Agent2Agent protocol and the Model Context Protocol.

Unlike a general agent communication framework, this project focuses specifically on cross-domain dialog recovery, gateway failure handling, authorization verification, and identifier privacy.

It is an independent research implementation and does not claim endorsement by, implementation of, or compliance with existing AAIF protocols.

Formal interoperability integrations remain future work.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Current demonstrated use cases include:

Recovery from mediator or gateway failures in multi-agent conversations.

Resumption using domain-specific identifiers.

Authorization checks during conversation recovery.

Prevention of duplicate or conflicting operations.

Reproducible failure-injection and privacy analysis.

The repository contains documented experimental scenarios, automated tests, and reproducible research outputs.

No independent production deployment or organizational adoption is currently verified. The project is being proposed for Sandbox consideration as an early-stage research implementation.

### Governance Model

The project is currently maintained independently by Nikhil Reddy Donapati.

Technical changes, issue prioritization, and release decisions are currently managed by the project maintainer.

A formal multi-maintainer governance structure has not yet been established. If accepted into AAIF, the project would work toward documented open governance and transparent contributor participation.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

The repository uses GitHub Actions to execute automated tests on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.

The workflow also runs a small experimental smoke test covering the research implementation.

The project includes Python package metadata, a changelog, and versioned research releases, currently at version 0.2.1.

An automated package publication workflow has not yet been verified.


### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

The project currently documents an experimental implementation and research analysis rather than maintaining a formally approved technical specification.

A dedicated specification contribution process has not yet been established.

The proposed future process is to discuss technical changes through public GitHub issues, submit implementation and documentation changes through pull requests, and require regression tests for changes to security-sensitive behavior.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/nikhilred2619/agentproto-privacy-preserving-dialog-recovery/issues

Verify that GitHub Issues is enabled before submitting.

### External Project Dependencies

The implementation requires Python 3.11 or newer.

Its declared runtime dependency is the Python cryptography package (version 42 or newer), which is available under Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause licensing.

Pytest is an optional development dependency for automated testing.

Dependency licensing and any additional transitive dependencies should be reviewed before foundation onboarding.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The maintainer manages research direction, implementation, testing, documentation, and release decisions.

Future governance development would focus on transparent issue discussions, contributor review processes, documented decision-making, and recruiting additional maintainers.

### Roadmap

Proposed 12-month roadmap, subject to available resources and authorization to perform the work:

Months 1–3: Improve contributor documentation, security reporting procedures, test coverage, and reproducibility instructions.

Months 4–6: Develop additional agent communication recovery scenarios and interoperability experiments.

Months 7–9: Expand failure-injection testing, authorization scenarios, and reproducible performance benchmarks.

Months 10–12: Seek external technical feedback, independent reproduction, and community contributions. Publish a documented evaluation of observed limitations and results.

### Security

The research implementation includes authorization-state checks, cryptographically protected recovery material, persistent operation tracking, and regression tests for previously identified failure cases.

Security-sensitive behaviors are evaluated through controlled experiments, including failure injection and invalid recovery scenarios.

The implementation is a research prototype and should not be represented as production-hardened or independently certified.

A formal SECURITY.md disclosure policy and additional independent security review remain desirable future improvements.

No OpenSSF Best Practices badge is currently claimed.
